*PharmaCraft Daily - 08 Nov 2026*

🎓 *MBBS* (Hematology)
Q: Heparin acts by enhancing the activity of?
Ans: Antithrombin III
Why: Heparin potentiates antithrombin III, inactivating thrombin and factor Xa; monitored by aPTT.

🌍 *FMGE* (Hematology)
Q: Low-molecular-weight heparin (enoxaparin) mainly inhibits?
Ans: Factor Xa
Why: LMWH preferentially inhibits factor Xa (via antithrombin); more predictable, given subcutaneously.

🩺 *NEET PG* (Hematology)
Q: Idarucizumab is the specific reversal agent for?
Ans: Dabigatran
Why: Idarucizumab is a monoclonal antibody fragment that rapidly reverses the thrombin inhibitor dabigatran.

🏥 *INI-CET* (Hematology)
Q: Why is bridging with heparin needed when starting warfarin in acute thrombosis?
Ans: Warfarin is slow and initially prothrombotic (protein C falls first)
Why: Warfarin first lowers protein C (short half-life), causing transient hypercoagulability; heparin bridges this.

🔬 *MD Pharmacology* (Paper IV: Recent Advances)
Q: Tirzepatide is novel because it is a dual agonist of?
Ans: GIP and GLP-1 receptors
Why: Tirzepatide is a dual GIP/GLP-1 receptor agonist with potent glucose-lowering and weight-loss effects.
